ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: the figure is a schematic cross-section of a mountain area, with undulating hillsides and valley positions, and it marks the “shaded area,” indicating that the object of discussion is the mountain slope surface and its catchment environment. Then reason: hillside vegetation can intercept precipitation, promote infiltration, conserve soil and water, and conserve water sources, and has a regulating effect on river runoff. If hillside vegetation is excessively cut down, surface runoff in the rainy season or snowmelt period will flow into the river faster and more concentratedly, and the flow in the high-water period will increase; in the low-water period, because groundwater recharge decreases, river flow will decline. Therefore the river will be fuller in the high-water period and drier in the low-water period, and the seasonal variation of runoff will increase.
